short: M06 ahead for 2012: no earlier heard-speech reconstruction in the ledger, repeated over 15 patients. Word readout rests on one patient; later vocoder targets beat the linear design by listeners.
position: The paper [@pasley2012] changes the decoding target (M06), reconstructing heard speech from human STG as a linear auditory spectrogram and as temporal-modulation energy. This is ahead for 2012: no study in the ledger's 64-study heard-speech reconstruction population predates it, the read human priors classified syllable responses [@chang2010] or decoded formants during attempted speech [@guenther2009], and the linear-versus-modulation comparison is repeated across 15 participants (F(1,14) = 33.36). The evaluation (M12), Pearson r plus an identification rank, is standard. The single-trial word readout overreaches: one participant, 47 candidates from one speaker, median rank 0.76, and a smoothing width chosen as best without stated selection data. Intelligibility was not measured; [later] work found the linear spectrogram design to be the baseline, with vocoder-parameter decoding 67% better by listeners [@akbari2019].
